content:
Key observations: Leaves show a white/gray powdery coating predominantly on the upper leaf surface. The leaves themselves appear otherwise green but are covered with what looks like a dusty white film. This strongly suggests Powdery Mildew.

Let me confirm with reference images.

The Cercospora reference shows purple/dark discoloration — very different from the test image. The Powdery Mildew reference is a perfect match: white/gray powdery fungal growth covering the upper leaf surfaces, giving leaves a dusty white/silver appearance identical to the test image.

```json
{"prediction": "Powdery_Mildew", "confidence": 0.95, "reasoning": "The test image shows a characteristic white/gray powdery coating uniformly covering the upper leaf surfaces of soybean plants. This dusty, whitish film on the upper surface is the hallmark sign of Powdery Mildew (white powdery fungal growth). The reference collage for Powdery_Mildew shows an identical appearance. Cercospora was ruled out (shows purple/dark spotting), and Downy Mildew was ruled out (different appearance, primarily affects pods/seeds internally)."}
```
